issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSongVerse has conflicting access modifiers across artifacts: the UML in the problem statement (Farm - singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal):void) and the template implementation declare singFarmSongVerse as private, whereas the reference solution declares it as protected (protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)). This difference can confuse students about the intended visibility and may cause unexpected access issues (for example, if tests or package-level helpers expect protected access). Files showing the conflict: problem_statement.md (UML) and template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declare private; solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares protected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution method to private (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) to match the UML/template, or (B) update the UML and the template to declare singFarmSongVerse as protected and add a short note in the problem text explaining why protected is used (e.g., to allow package-level or subclass testing). Apply the same chosen visibility to the template code, the UML in problem_statement.md, and the reference solution so students are not left reconciling conflicting access modifiers.
